note: Structural templates only — hook shapes, skeletons, and render presets. No brand values live here; every template is filled from Business/[slug]/context/ at runtime.

templates.name: The price gap
templates.when: You want to qualify budget without stating a price, and take a position on how competitors quote.
templates.hook: Two [quotes/bids/proposals] for the same [thing] came in $[N] apart.
skeleton: Hook: the gap, as a specific number
The assumption most people make about the gap, and why it's wrong
The actual mechanism, with 2-3 concrete specifics
Where the cost reappears later, and why leverage is gone by then
The one question that closes the gap

templates.name: What's behind the wall
templates.when: Expertise post. Show what a professional sees that the buyer can't.
templates.hook: [N] years of [problem] were hiding behind one [ordinary thing].
skeleton: Hook: the discovery, specific and physical
What the business saw and fell in love with
What you saw at the same moment
Why no inspection or walkthrough catches it
The process change that protects them

templates.name: Before you even start
templates.when: Reset expectations on how long something really takes. Filters tire-kickers.
templates.hook: [N] weeks before you [obvious first step everyone pictures].
skeleton: Hook: the number nobody expects
What that time is actually spent on
Why skipping it costs more than it saves
What a realistic sequence looks like
What to ask before signing anything

templates.name: The unpopular opinion
templates.when: You hold a professional view most of your market disagrees with. Highest polarity, highest comment volume.
templates.hook: Everyone wants [popular thing]. We talk most businesses out of it.
skeleton: Hook: state the position flatly, no hedging
Acknowledge honestly why the popular view is appealing
The specific case where it fails
What you recommend instead, and for whom
Invite disagreement

templates.name: We turn work down
templates.when: Premium positioning. Only usable when the scarcity is real — never manufacture it.
templates.hook: We turn down more [inquiries/projects] than we take on.
skeleton: Hook: the ratio, stated without apology
The specific reasons a project gets declined
Why taking it anyway would hurt the business, not just you
Who it IS right for
A low-friction way to find out which they are

templates.name: The first question I ask
templates.when: Authority through qualification. Teaches your process while filtering.
templates.hook: The first question I ask every [client type] is [question].
skeleton: Hook: the question itself
Why it sounds trivial
What the answer actually reveals
What each kind of answer leads to
Soft invitation to answer it themselves

templates.name: You don't need X, you need Y
templates.when: Cut through category hype. Replaces an intimidating abstraction with a concrete cheap action.
templates.hook: You don't need [expensive abstract thing]. You need [small concrete thing].
skeleton: Hook: the swap, stated plainly
Why the abstract version is what everyone sells
The three concrete things that actually matter
Name them specifically, in the reader's own vocabulary
The smallest possible next step

templates.name: It wasn't the finish
templates.when: Lifestyle and aspiration. The emotional counterweight to education-heavy weeks.
templates.hook: It wasn't the [luxury detail]. It was [the quiet, human outcome].
skeleton: Hook: reject the obvious luxury signal
The moment that actually mattered, described physically
What made that moment possible, structurally
Why that's what you're really buying
Understated invitation

templates.name: News hook, translated
templates.when: A real, checkable news item in your space. Timely, and the easiest recurring pillar to sustain.
templates.hook: [Specific, verifiable thing that just happened].
skeleton: Hook: the news, stated concretely with the real detail
Why it sounds irrelevant to a small business
The specific way it touches their week
What to actually do about it
One-line takeaway
templates.warning: Only use with a real, verifiable source. Never invent the news item or its numbers.

templates.name: I use this myself
templates.when: You have no case studies yet. The strongest proof available pre-testimonial, and structurally uncopyable.
templates.hook: [Specific thing you did in your own business this week].
skeleton: Hook: the real thing you did, with the real detail
The problem it solved, in hours or dollars
How you actually set it up
What it would look like in their business
Offer to show them

templates.name: N things before you X
templates.when: Highest-saving carousel shape. Educational, easy to skim, easy to share.
templates.hook: [N] things you should know before you [big irreversible decision].
skeleton: Slide 1: hook with the number
Slides 2-6: one item per slide, each a specific and slightly surprising claim
Final slide: what to do first, plus CTA

templates.name: What $X vs $Y gets you
templates.when: Budget education. Qualifies hard and pre-empts sticker shock.
templates.hook: What $[low] / $[mid] / $[high] actually gets you in [market].
skeleton: Slide 1: the three numbers
One slide per tier: what's included, what isn't, who it fits
Slide on the mistake people make choosing between them
Final slide: how to find your tier

templates.name: One objection per slide
templates.when: You keep hearing the same hesitation on sales calls. Answer it once, publicly.
templates.hook: "[The objection, in their exact words]."
skeleton: Slide 1: the objection quoted verbatim
Slide 2: agree with the part that's fair
Slides 3-5: the specific counter-evidence, one per slide
Final slide: the low-risk way to test it

templates.name: Stage by stage
templates.when: Demystify what happens after someone hires you. Reduces the fear of the unknown.
templates.hook: What actually happens between [signing] and [finishing].
skeleton: Slide 1: the two endpoints and the gap between them
One slide per real stage, named the way you name it internally
Note on where businesses usually get anxious and what you do about it
Final slide: where to start

templates.name: We're not for everyone
templates.when: Positioning piece. Run once or twice a year, not monthly — it loses force with repetition.
templates.hook: We're not for everyone.
skeleton: Slide 1: the statement, alone
Slides 2-4: who this is genuinely not for, stated without contempt
Slide 5: who it is for, specifically
Final slide: an honest way to self-select

templates.name: Offer announcement
templates.when: Launching or filling something with limited capacity. Earns the pitch before making it.
templates.hook: [Contrarian reframe of the problem the offer solves].
skeleton: Slide 1: hook — reframe, don't announce
Slide 2: the problem, in their language
Slide 3: the idea in one sentence
Slide 4: specificity — name real examples, not categories
Slide 5: proof you have (yours, if no businesses yet)
Slide 6: the format — what it actually is
Slide 7: the price and the constraint, with the reason for the constraint
Slide 8: the honest next step
templates.warning: If no date, price, or capacity is actually confirmed, the CTA is a waitlist — never a fabricated deadline.

templates.name: AIDA short form
templates.when: Cold paid traffic. The default paid structure.
templates.hook: [Specific number, bold claim, or status hook] — stop the scroll in 2 seconds.
skeleton: Attention: the specific hook
Interest: reveal the complexity, show you understand
Desire: the concrete transformation
Action: one friction-reduced CTA, scarcity only if real

templates.name: Number-first qualifier
templates.when: You need to filter unqualified leads at the ad level rather than in the inbox.
templates.hook: [Project type] in [place] starts around $[N]. Here's what that buys.
skeleton: Lead with the number — this is the filter
What's included at that level
What pushes it higher
CTA aimed only at people the number didn't scare

templates.name: Low-friction download
templates.when: Cold audience that isn't ready for a consultation ask.
templates.hook: The [document] we give every [client type] before they [decision].
skeleton: The asset, described as a real internal artifact
The three things it prevents
Who should not bother downloading it
Download CTA

templates.name: Project reveal
templates.when: You have real photography of a finished job. Highest-performing format when the images are genuinely good.
templates.hook: [The single most surprising fact about the transformation].
skeleton: Hook: the surprising constraint or discovery
What the space was, honestly
The one decision that changed everything
What it took to get there
Credit the business's nerve, not your own skill
templates.warning: Requires real photography. Never AI-generate an image depicting a real property or project.
